channel.title: Open Calls for Artists — Monographica
channel.description: Curated list of open calls for photographers and visual artists. Exhibitions, grants, residencies, and publications worldwide.

item.title: Pearl Press — Solo Issue Open Call
item.description: Pearl Press is an independent online publication, 28 issues deep, that normally runs themed group issues. The next one is different: the whole issue goes to a single photographer, or to a collaboration between two. The call asks for 20 to 30 pieces with a one-page bio and a description of the work, and sets no theme at all — 'there is no concept to adhere to', so the brief is simply a body of work you are proud of. The selected artist is interviewed inside the issue (both photographers, where two apply together) and promoted on the publication's Instagram. Submission is free and by email, with visual work at a minimum of 300 dpi; more than 30 pieces may be sent, though only part of what arrives will be used. The publication was founded by Delilah Twersky, a fine-arts photographer and creative writer who works primarily with medium-format film and whose own work has been published by Dashwood Books, Waif Magazine, Aint-Bad and Sissy Screens; Pearl Press itself has been interviewed by Chill Subs. — Deadline: October 25, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Solo issue publication with interview.

item.title: 2027 Student Showcase · Gresham Area League for the Arts
item.description: The Gresham Area League for the Arts' student show, hung in GALA's gallery in the Gresham City Council Chambers, Oregon, from 11 January to 19 February 2027 and opened with an artists' reception and award ceremony on 14 January. GALA invites students in grades 6 through 12 from the East County school districts and surrounding areas, and names photography directly alongside ceramics, digital art, drawing, fibre, glass, metalwork, mixed media, painting, printmaking, sculpture and wood; 2D and 3D work are both welcome. Reproducible work — computer-generated art, digitally altered photographs, giclee prints — must be labelled as such, and photographic prints must be signed, numbered as part of a limited edition and meet archival standards. Work must be entirely the student's own and made within the last year: no class step-out pieces, no paint-by-number. The gallery lends frames in four sizes (12x16, 12x18, 16x20 and 14x14) to students who need them and retains 20% commission on sales; submissions must stay clear of nudity, sexual content and divisive themes for a family-friendly multi-use space. Accepted work is delivered in person on 8 or 9 January and stays up for the whole run, with an art talk on 4 February and an education Saturday on 6 February. No entry fee is stated anywhere on the call page. Entries close at midnight on Wednesday 16 December 2026. — Deadline: December 16, 2026. Fee: See website. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: Portrait Series Open Call · SHOW LA
item.description: SHOW LA — the Los Angeles photography fair that runs 10–13 December 2026 at The Reef, 1933 S. Broadway — has partnered with LensCulture on an open call for portrait photography. Photographers of all categories and levels may submit a portrait series of up to ten images, which should sit within the same body of work or series; entries opened 6 October and close 30 October. The grand prize winner takes a $1,000 cash prize, a feature on SHOW LA's Instagram account and an exhibition at SHOW LA this December; three finalists are exhibited at the fair alongside the winner. The call is open internationally and is judged by three jurors — Paris Chong, gallery director of the Leica Store & Gallery Los Angeles, Ann M. Jastrab, executive director of the Center for Photographic Art, and Matthew Martin, director of the Peter Fetterman Gallery. Entry is $45 and submissions are handled on LensCulture, whose entry route requires a signed-in account. — Deadline: October 30, 2026. Fee: $45. Prize: $1,000 + exhibition at SHOW LA.

item.title: BROAD Magazine — Open Submissions
item.description: Independent visual-culture photography publication that features one photographer's project at a time on its website, with a short artist text alongside the pictures — recent features include Giovanni Fafoglia's Cellophane, Federica Nannini's Assenze silenziose on emptied high-school classrooms, Roberto Zeppilli's Fotosottocasa made entirely within walking distance of his home, and Sinziana Velicescu's Purgatory, Paradise on civic and commercial architecture across the American landscape. BROAD describes itself as a community-driven publication working with artists from around the world and says it is always open to submissions: there is no theme, no deadline and no fee on this route. Applicants fill in the form on the submissions page and supply a direct link to a gallery or folder of the images they want considered (Dropbox or Google Drive both fine). Because of the volume received, BROAD contacts photographers only if their submission is selected for publication. Note that BROAD's separate themed print issues run as their own open calls with their own paid community-membership route; this rolling route is for the website features. — Deadline: Continuous. Fee: Free. Prize: Publication.

item.title: What the Streets Hold · Decagon Gallery
item.description: Decagon Gallery's Spotlight open call for street photography, juried by the gallery's own Curator and Artistic Director, Teona Machavariani. The brief is about what people reveal without intending to — how they wait, protect themselves, occupy space, move toward one another, or remain separate while standing side by side — and the gallery is explicit that it is not after dramatic events, visual coincidences or perfectly timed gestures, but photographs that make you pause because something in them feels known even when you cannot explain what happened. Work may be made on streets, in stations, markets, public transport, neighbourhoods or anywhere strangers temporarily share a place; a person can be central, barely visible, or present only through what they have left behind. All photographic processes and styles are welcome, open to photographers worldwide over 18. Awards total $1,000 — $500 first place, $250 second, $150 third and two $50 honourable mentions, one cash award per photographer — plus a Human Presence Award giving free entry to a future Decagon exhibition. Selected artists get an online exhibition, publication in a professionally designed exhibition catalog, and digital badges and certificates. Photographers retain all rights including copyright; the gallery takes the right to publish selected work in the exhibition, the catalog and promotion. Entry is $25 for up to four photographs and $5 for each additional, and the entry form carries ten upload slots. Exhibition runs February 10 – April 10, 2027. — Deadline: January 15, 2027. Fee: $25 (4 images) + $5 each additional. Prize: $1,000 in awards + Exhibition.

item.title: FOTODOKS Open Call 2027
item.description: FOTODOKS, the biennial festival for contemporary documentary photography in Munich, is building the central group exhibition of its thirteenth edition (October 2027) from an open call on care — care as emotional, physical, psychological, social and relational work, and its entanglement with politics, labour, ethics and intimate relationships at a moment when 'community' and 'belonging' circulate as branded buzzwords. The festival seeks existing lens-based, documentary-driven stories of care with a photorealistic and honest intention, asking how documentary photography meets today's imaginaries of care after the dismantling of welfare-state models and the rise of 'self-care' as a slogan for overworked bodies. Submit one project of 5-10 images, in English or German; individuals, duos and collectives are all eligible, and the curatorial team also extends direct invitations alongside the open call. Selected artists receive an artist fee of EUR 500 (EUR 800 for duos, up to EUR 1,200 for collectives), a travel budget of up to EUR 150 within Germany, EUR 300 within Europe or EUR 500 from outside Europe, accommodation for the four-day opening week, full production of the work for the exhibition, inclusion in the festival catalogue with five printed copies, and a presentation on the FOTODOKS website. FOTODOKS encourages applicants of all ethnic backgrounds, religions, ages, genders, disabilities, sexual orientations and social statuses, does not sell exhibited work, and leaves copyright with the artist. Results early spring 2027. — Deadline: November 20, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: €500 artist fee + Exhibition.

item.title: SPACE: Exterus Spatium · Crooked Tree Arts Center
item.description: Juried exhibition in the Carnegie and Cornwell Galleries at Crooked Tree Arts Center in Traverse City, Michigan, on outer space: the moon, the planets, the stars, solar systems, galaxies and beyond, or their effects on our Earth. Science fact and science fiction are equally encouraged, and work may be literal or abstract, traditional or experimental, miniature or monumental. All media are welcome except AI; photography and telescopic images are eligible as long as the image was solely captured and reproduced by the artist. Open to US residents 18+, up to three works completed within the last three years. $30 entry, $20 for CTAC members, free for Guild members. Notification 4 December 2026; exhibition 15 January - 27 February 2027. The galleries are sales galleries and CTAC retains a 40% commission on sales; work need not be for sale. — Deadline: November 30, 2026. Fee: $30 ($20 members). Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: RBSA Photography Prize 2027
item.description: The Royal Birmingham Society of Artists' biennial photography prize, open to anyone working with any photographic process, anywhere. The RBSA is one of the oldest art societies in the country and only admitted photography into the Society in October 2022; this is the third show since that decision, and for the third time it expands to fill both Gallery 1 and Gallery 2 in the Society's Birmingham gallery. Professional and emerging artists based locally, nationally and internationally are all invited, and all photographic styles and media are eligible — work may be photography or digitally manipulated photography, and both 2D and 3D works are accepted, including installation pieces. Selection is by digital image of the original artwork only, and every entry goes through the same anonymous process judged on the quality and interest of the work; the selection panel is listed as TBC on both the call page and the exhibition pack. Three cash prizes are awarded — the John Hodgett Award of £1,000, a second prize of £500 sponsored by Judd Medical, and the Anne Judd Award of £250 — plus up to six Highly Commended certificates, and a catalogue featuring all selected works is published alongside the exhibition. Artists may enter up to four pieces in total. Entry costs £20 for one work rising to £48 for four, halved for artists under 35 (who must telephone the Gallery to pay at that rate) and free for RBSA Honorary Members and Next Generation RBSA Artists. Photographers should read the entry requirements closely: all work must be original, any manipulation must have been carried out by the artist, images created using AI are not accepted, work must have been made in the past three years and must not have been shown at the RBSA Gallery before, and all prints including digital ones must be editioned with the edition size stated. Image files must be JPG, at least 2,000 pixels across the smallest dimension at 300dpi. Work is to be framed unless an unframed presentation is intrinsic to the piece, works over 1.5m in any dimension must be discussed with the Gallery after submission, and artists supply and PAT-test their own equipment for video works. Sold work carries a 35% commission plus VAT. The exhibition runs Thursday 25 February to Saturday 20 March 2027, with a preview evening on the opening night. — Deadline: January 5, 2027. Fee: £20 one entry / £32 two / £40 three / £48 four; 50% off for artists under 35; free for RBSA Honorary Members and Next Generation RBSA Artists. Prize: £1,000 / £500 / £250 + Exhibition.

item.title: SoulScapes — Artdoc Magazine Open Call · Artdoc Photography Magazine
item.description: An international open call from Artdoc Photography Magazine on spirituality, inner awareness and the invisible dimensions of human experience. The magazine frames spirituality broadly — found in nature, silence, contemplation, personal rituals and moments of heightened awareness — and asks for work about the search for meaning and our relationship with experience beyond the visible world: inner experiences, intuition, memory, emotion, and the importance of feeling, observing, questioning and reflecting. Art and documentary photography, visual diaries and visual storytelling are all welcome, as is work that reaches the invisible through light, atmosphere, symbol, abstraction and experiment; the editors say they are interested in the relationship between inner and outer worlds rather than in one register of image-making. Selected work is shown in Artdoc's international online exhibition or published in the magazine, and selected photographers may be invited for a portfolio interview. Submission is through a member-only form on the call page: entry itself costs nothing, but you must hold an Artdoc membership, €35 a year (the magazine's membership page currently offers a first year at €24 with the coupon ARTDOC50%), which also carries the six digital issues and the member-only submission forms. The call page itself prints “This Open Call is Now Closed” to visitors who are not signed in — the same line appears word for word on Artdoc’s past calls, while the magazine’s own open-calls page lists SoulScapes as its current open call with this deadline, and the submission form only appears once you are logged in as a member. Photographers keep copyright; submitting grants Artdoc permission to publish the images in its online exhibitions, features, issues, social channels and promotional material. The magazine states it may refuse entries that fall outside its ethical and aesthetic parameters, naming explicit nudity and overtly submissive postures as likely refusals. — Deadline: November 23, 2026. Fee: Free (Artdoc membership required, €35/year). Prize: Publication / online exhibition.

item.title: Artist Studios 2027 · International Centre for the Image
item.description: PhotoIreland offers four year-long studio spaces at the International Centre for the Image, its cultural space in Dublin supported by the Arts Council of Ireland, for the period January to December 2027. The studios sit in the centre's Atelier, a spacious sound-panelled room with a workshop area and a well-equipped kitchenette, laid out as a shared open studio for four artists; each workspace has a sit-stand adjustable desk, an ergonomic chair and a generous set of shelves. Studio artists also get regular, easy access to the centre's art library, art bookshop and staff, and can use the studio seven days a week during opening hours. The studio comes at no cost to the artist, and PhotoIreland provides a bursary of up to €1,000 reimbursable against materials; studio artists are required to take part in studio visits and talk programmes and are paid for that time. In exchange the centre asks for a real commitment: use of the facilities at least three days a week, for the whole January–December 2027 period — studios are not offered for shorter terms, and failing the three-day commitment means losing the space. Open to photographers and visual artists based in Ireland, at any level of practice from recent graduate to established; any visual arts discipline is welcome, though the setup suits desk-based practices best. The centre is wheelchair accessible and artists with all access needs are welcome, with specific requirements noted in the submission; because the studios and workshop are shared open-plan, applicants are asked to keep their future studio-mates' varied practices in mind. PhotoIreland is a signatory to the Safe to Create Code of Behaviour. Apply in two steps: complete the online Google Form, then send one PDF of no more than 10 MB containing a CV and artist statement, a concise statement of motivation setting out how you would use and benefit from the studio, an outline of previous projects (linked or embedded) and any specific requirements you foresee. Multiple files are not processed and submissions that deviate from the process are not considered. The call opened 5 October 2026, submissions are reviewed 15–30 November, artists are contacted between 1 and 13 December 2026, and studio residencies commence 4 January 2027. The organisers state plainly that they do not extend deadlines. The call is planned to be annual and past studio artists may reapply. — Deadline: November 15, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Studio space + €1,000 bursary.

item.title: PhotoIreland FUTURES Talents 2027
item.description: Tenth edition of the FUTURES Talent Call run by PhotoIreland as the Irish member of the FUTURES Photography Platform, the Creative Europe-funded network that since 2017 has pooled the talent programmes of leading European photography institutions — 23 members as of 2026, among them Der Greif, FOMU, Foto Arsenal Wien, FOTODOK, Fotofestiwal Lodz, Photo Elysée, Fundació Foto Colectania, ISSP, Organ Vida, Triennial of Photography Hamburg and Void. Free to enter and open to artists based in Ireland and the UK, as well as Irish and UK artists practising abroad; the call takes photography and its expanded practice at any level, and the jury is explicitly looking for contemporary lens-based artists regardless of curriculum or experience who have shown dedication and serious intent in their practice. Selected artists receive a participation fee of €500; Futures Conversations with international professionals, online and in person; covered travel, accommodation and per diem for the FUTURES Annual Event, which in 2027 takes place in October in Vienna hosted by Foto Arsenal Wien, with the talks and workshops programme included; the chance to apply to the internal open call for the annual travelling exhibition, curated in 2027 by Foto Arsenal Wien, Fotofestiwal Lodz and the Finnish Museum of Photography; the chance to apply for a mentorship session with a FUTURES member organisation; access to Magnum workshops developed for FUTURES artists; an artist page on futures-photography.com; and promotion through the platform's channels and the annual publication, which in 2027 marks the network's tenth anniversary. PhotoIreland has put 45 artists forward to date, among them Ciarán Óg Arnold, Megan Doherty, Miriam O'Connor, Róisín White, Vera Ryklova and Yvette Monahan. Apply by emailing a single PDF containing a 200-word third-person bio, an artist statement, a CV, a description of your latest project in up to 500 words, a selection of low-resolution images from that project and brief information on past projects; receipt is acknowledged within two working days. Selected artists then supply fifteen flattened TIFFs at 300 dpi, 4500 px on the long side, plus a portrait, due by 17 January 2027. The jury sits from 30 November to 20 December 2026 and all applicants are contacted before 10 January 2027. The organisers state plainly that they do not extend deadlines. — Deadline: November 27, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: €500 + FUTURES platform membership + Travel covered.

item.title: un/fund 05 — Publishing Open Call · un/fund
item.description: Fifth edition of un/fund, the open call run by un/produced — a non-profit production company and artist consultancy registered in Amsterdam and Paris — which has reinvested over €200,000 into un/signed and un/represented artists since 2022. This edition turns one photographer's body of work into a first photobook: the book is fully funded by un/produced and published in collaboration with Witty Books, the Turin independent press founded by Tommaso Parrillo in 2012, which works with artists through sequencing, rhythm, material and tactile form rather than handing back a finished template. The selected photographer receives complete financial support, so production costs are eliminated, plus professional guidance through every phase of the publishing journey, from image editing and sequencing to material design and distribution, and joins the un/fund community with promotion across the un/fund and un/produced networks. There is no set theme. Projects may be finished or still in progress and no book dummy is required; the organisers say explicitly that they welcome experimentation, critical thinking and a commitment to exploring underrepresented or overlooked narratives, and that no prior book-making or publishing experience is needed. Open internationally to photographers — including creative duos, where only one member applies on behalf of both — who have no ongoing gallery or agency representation, have up to seven years of professional practice and have not yet published a photobook, where a self-published zine does not count. The seven years are counted from your first exhibition, publication or paid commission rather than from when you first picked up a camera, and career breaks for parental leave, illness or caring responsibilities are not counted; showing in group exhibitions or selling prints yourself does not count as representation. One project per application, one application per photographer, up to 30 images with a project statement and a short biography, all materials in English. Entry is €10. Submissions opened 19 October 2026 and close 17 November 2026 at 23:59 GMT. Shortlisted applicants are contacted in December 2026 and the winner is announced shortly after. The organisers cannot give individual feedback on applications. — Deadline: November 17, 2026. Fee: €10. Prize: Publication.

item.title: Kota Sepi Kota Sunyi · Tiga Mata
item.description: Tiga Mata, the Malaysian photography zine published by Zontiga, invites photographers across Southeast Asia to photograph quietness, solitude, silence and emptiness in the urban environment. The call extends the thinking behind Ahmad Zakii Anwar's Kota Sepi and Kota Sunyi — two bodies of work about Johor Bahru, the city of his birth, shown in the exhibition Sementara at GDP Campus — outward to Kuala Lumpur, Bangkok, Jakarta, Manila, Singapore, Hanoi, Phnom Penh and anywhere else in the region. In Malay kota means city, while sepi leans towards solitude, loneliness or a place deserted and sunyi towards silence and stillness; the organisers deliberately refuse to fix either word to a single English translation. They are explicit that silence need not mean the absence of people — solitude can exist among thousands — and that they want work made from spending time with a place rather than illustrating a word. Up to five photographs with a project statement, an account of process and intent, and disclosure of image sources where applicable; JPEG, sRGB, 3000 pixels on the longest side. Selected photographs are curated by Zontiga into a physical exhibition at Level 1, Testing Ground, GDP Campus, running 19 December 2026 to 1 February 2027 during the final period of Sementara, with printing and production costs covered by the organisers and no further fee for selected photographers. Open to amateurs and professionals who are nationals of Brunei, Cambodia, Indonesia, Laos, Malaysia, Myanmar, the Philippines, Singapore, Thailand, Timor-Leste or Vietnam; applicants under 16 need a guardian's written consent. Copyright stays with the photographer, who grants a non-exclusive licence for exhibition and promotion of the project. Results are announced 19 November 2026. — Deadline: November 8, 2026. Fee: RM 30. Prize: Group exhibition.

item.title: The Scenic Route: Reimagining Highway 250 · Lanesboro Arts
item.description: Project grants of $500–$1,500 for artist-led activations of downtown Lanesboro, a small Minnesota town in Fillmore County whose main street — Highway 250 — is dug up through 2027–28 for water, sewer, roadway, sidewalk, lighting and trail work. Lanesboro Arts, which has worked in the town for over four decades and whose city council in 2014 declared the whole town an Arts Campus, is funding between 10 and 20 projects to "change the narrative from one of uncertainty to one of opportunity" while the construction runs. WHAT COUNTS AS A PROJECT: "their own artistic activation of the space, whether through installation, performance, or other creative programming" — the organisation's own examples run from "creating an art installation, hosting an artful picnic, throwing a dance party, offering a new point of view on construction, or something else creative". Photography is not named as a medium on either surface and the award is for a public activation rather than for a body of pictures; the organisation's own gallery calls do state "All visual arts media are eligible". A photographer's route in is therefore a project sited downtown: documenting the dig and the people living through it, a street-level installation of prints, a participatory portrait session, a projection. Proposals are judged on their potential to engage Lanesboro, logistical feasibility, and fit with four stated goals — connection, beauty and pride downtown; visitors and residents stopping, shopping and lingering; collaboration across sectors amid the disruption; and conversation about construction, maintenance and building Lanesboro's future. WHO CAN APPLY: "the application is open to artists and community members. An established art practice is not required." There is no geographic bar, but "Priority will be given to residents of Fillmore County, as well as BIPOC, LGBTQIA+, and/or disabled individuals" — and the work has to happen in downtown Lanesboro between April and October 2027, which is the practical limit. Free to apply, by a form on the organisation's own site asking for a brief project proposal with intended location, audience, goals and timeline. The priority deadline is 15 January 2027 at 11:59 pm; after that "Rolling applications will be accepted until project funds are depleted". Lanesboro Arts runs supporting workshops around the call, and the application page says applicants are "highly encouraged" to have attended one of the Civic Arts Engagement Workshops: a virtual Civic Arts Engagement Workshop with Springboard for the Arts on 12 November, Creative Idea Development round tables on 22 October and 13 December at the Sylvan Brewing Scale Room, and Creative Project Support round tables on 18 February and 14 March 2027. The partners named are the Minnesota Department of Transportation and UMN Extension. — Deadline: January 15, 2027. Fee: Free. Prize: $500–$1,500 project grant.

item.title: Guest Exhibition Submissions · ViewPoint Gallery
item.description: Standing call for guest exhibitions at ViewPoint Gallery, "an artist-run co-operative" at 1475 Bedford Highway in Bedford, Nova Scotia, founded in July 2000 as a collaboration between photographers and printmakers and focused on fine art photography exclusively since 2006. It shows monthly exhibitions and has hosted over 250 of them, and it fills roughly one guest slot a year: "In addition to the solo shows there is one guest exhibition and several group exhibitions shown each year." THIS IS A SELF-PROPOSED EXHIBITION, NOT A THEMED GROUP CALL. The submission page says "ViewPoint Gallery welcomes submissions for solo shows", but the gallery's own SHOW YOUR WORK page says it "welcomes submissions for solo and group shows by guest artists" and the guidelines ask that "If the applicant is a group of photographers, samples of each artist’s work is necessary" — so a collective can apply. The applicant picks which of three parts of the gallery to use, with wall runs of 34'9", 29' or 20', walls 10' high, lit by natural light and 3000K LED. WHAT IT COSTS: nothing to apply, but a "$150 non-refundable exhibition fee" falls due on confirmation of the exhibition date — it pays for posters and vinyl lettering — and the exhibitor also carries shipping, insurance and all import duties, charges and taxes in both directions. The gallery says plainly that "As a non-profit organization the Gallery is unable to pay artist fees", and that work on its walls is not insured. WHAT THE EXHIBITOR DOES: prepare and print the images, take part in the installation, remove the work immediately after the close, cater the opening reception and give an artist talk — normally 2 pm on the second Sunday after the opening, in person or virtual. The gallery supports poster and promotional design, promotes the show on its site and social channels, hosts the opening, facilitates the talk and staffs the space during gallery hours. TIMELINE AFTER ACCEPTANCE: fee plus a 2–3 sentence statement and 3–4 images within 30 days; final selection, printing and layout 3–6 months before opening; window-poster images at 3 months; press kit at 2 months; rack-card images at 7 weeks; work arrives 2 weeks before opening. WHAT TO SEND: exhibition title and a 150–250-word artist statement; bio or CV; 10–20 images as work prints (minimum 8x10 inches) or digital files (maximum 1920 by 1080 pixels, sRGB); an image list giving title, year, medium and framed and unframed dimensions; 4–8 exhibition-quality prints of at least 8x10 inches, which need not be the works proposed; and a description of the printing, framing and matting method plus the proposed installation, number of works, space required and any unusual requirements. Packages must be mailed or dropped off in person during opening hours, and without a self-addressed envelope carrying Canadian postage or International Reply Coupons the gallery disposes of submission materials rather than returning them. A group of photographers must include samples of each artist's work. The Programming Committee accepts or declines; the gallery's board holds final authority. The deadline is March 15 for the next calendar year and "Submissions are not reviewed before this date." Among the content questions the gallery asks applicants to work through: "Have you used generative AI in the creation of any of your images? Is so, please describe extent and purpose of usage." — Deadline: March 15, 2027. Fee: Free ($150 exhibition fee if accepted). Prize: Solo or group exhibition.

item.title: Prime Desert Woodland Preserve Artist in Residence Program · Lancaster Museum of Art and History
item.description: A 12-week residency, 1 March to 23 May 2027, in the Prime Desert Woodland Preserve — high desert riparian woodland with Joshua trees, native wildlife and seasonal wildflowers on the edge of Lancaster, in California's Antelope Valley. The programme is run by the Lancaster Museum of Art and History (MOAH), which lists the Elyze Clifford Interpretive Center inside the Preserve among its sites. Photography is named in the prospectus among the media supported: "artists working across all media, including but not limited to visual arts, photography, writing, sound, performance, social practice, and interdisciplinary work." WHAT THE ARTIST GETS: a $1,500 stipend, hotel stays coordinated with the visiting schedule — the prospectus states the cap twice and disagrees with itself, "up to six" in the Residency Overview and "up to eight" under Accommodation and Working Conditions — studio access at the Cedar Creative Incubator in downtown Lancaster for the duration, access to the Preserve for research and observation, curatorial and logistical support from museum staff, promotion through museum channels, and a public exhibition at MOAH:CEDAR running 5 June to 1 August 2027, developed with MOAH's curatorial team. WHAT IS ASKED IN RETURN: approximately 8–12 documented visits to the Preserve across the 12 weeks, an anticipated visitation schedule agreed with staff before the residency begins, a simple residency log, at least one proposed and delivered community engagement activity (artist talk, workshop, guided walk or participatory programming) at MOAH:CEDAR or the Interpretive Center during the exhibition, and a Field Guide documenting the residency, due 1 October 2027. Two project boards at the Interpretive Center are available as working space for sketches, photographs, notes and maps during the residency. WHO CAN APPLY: emerging and established artists aged 18 and over who live in one of ten Southern California counties — Los Angeles, San Luis Obispo, Santa Barbara, Kern, Ventura, San Bernardino, Orange, Riverside, San Diego and Imperial. No prior environmental or ecological subject matter is required, but MOAH asks for a proposed direction of inquiry rather than a predetermined finished project. Artists who have held a solo exhibition at MOAH, MOAH:CEDAR, the Western Hotel Museum or the Elyze Clifford Interpretive Center within the last three years are not eligible. SUBMIT: statement of intent, a proposed community engagement activity (max 2,000 characters), a CV of up to two pages and work samples — five labelled images for visual artists, 3–5 pages for writers, 5–10 minute excerpts for time-based work — through CaFÉ by 20 November 2026. Entry fee $3; notification the week of 11 January 2027. Artists should be prepared for extreme desert heat, cold and wind on site. — Deadline: November 20, 2026. Fee: $3. Prize: $1,500 stipend + Residency + Exhibition.

item.title: The Artist of the Year Award 2026 · Arts to Hearts Project
item.description: Arts to Hearts Project's annual Artist of the Year Award selects 100 artists for a collectible printed book, from which one receives the top award. This edition is guest curated by Jennifer Rizzo. The award package is $500 in cash, a trophy, a certificate, a dedicated four-page feature in the book, and the project's PR and marketing push. Photography is one of the named categories alongside painting, ceramics, sculpture, installation, drawing and mixed media, so photographic work competes against the whole field rather than in a lane of its own; the organisers frame the book as an attempt to gather, in one place, a considered selection of artists working at the same moment rather than the fragments a viewer usually encounters. Entry is open to artists aged 18 and above anywhere in the world, and the fee is a ladder priced by how many works you send: $21 for one image, $35 for three, $47 for five, $62 for ten and $100 for twenty — so the cheapest serious entry is $21 and the cost per image falls steeply at the top of the ladder. Work must be the artist's own and available for publication if selected, and must come with accurate artwork details. AI-generated artwork is not eligible for this edition. One optional extra sits in the application form: $27 buys a customised artist interview published on the Arts to Hearts site with promotion across its social channels, run only if you are selected and non-refundable — it is an upsell, not a requirement, and it does not affect selection. The call runs from the apply.artstoheartsproject.com form, which carries the full prospectus; the organisation's own domain also publishes an announcement page for this edition at artstoheartsproject.com/artist-of-the-year-open-for-submissions/, which repeats the November 15 deadline, the guest curator and the award package but prints no fee. — Deadline: November 15, 2026. Fee: $21–$100 (tiered, 1–20 images). Prize: $500 + Publication + 4-page feature.

item.title: 5th Annual Black Artists Exhibit · Riverside Arts Center
item.description: Riverside Arts Center's fifth annual Black Artists Exhibit runs in honour of Martin Luther King Jr. Day, hosted with Ronnie and Gloria Peterson, the African American Cultural and Historical Museum of Washtenaw County, the Palm Leaf Club and Sankofa. All art mediums are welcome, so photography sits alongside painting, sculpture and fibre, and entry costs nothing — the call page says all RAC calls for art are free to apply and the centre's Artist Opportunities page says all of its calls for art are always free to enter. The geography is written as a preference, not a bar: open to artists locally, regionally and nationally, with priority possibly given to artists based in south-eastern Michigan, because the centre also wants work from outside the region that broadens the experience for its local community. Age is no bar either, though an artist under 18 needs written permission from a parent or guardian, who also co-signs any exhibition or sales agreement. Submissions run through Artwork Archive; the centre caps a submission at three artworks and the form asks for one to five images at 300 dpi and up to 5 MB each, an artist statement of up to 100 words and a bio of up to 50. Work must arrive display-ready — framed, wired or otherwise prepared — and no larger than 36 by 48 inches unless pre-approved, and anything previously exhibited at Riverside may not be resubmitted. The AI rules sit in two blocks that do not say the same thing. The eligibility criteria say work “created wholly or partially with AI tools must be disclosed at submission” and “will be evaluated under the same criteria as other submissions”, while Rules and Terms clause 2 says the centre “will not accept artwork that uses generative AI to create or assist in the creation of images, designs, text, or other creative content, whether in whole or in part”, and that disclosure is required even where the AI use is not generative, in which case it “does not automatically disqualify the work from consideration”. The narrower reading is the one to apply: generative AI is out, including as an assist, and any other AI tool used at any stage of design, editing or production has to be described in the application. The show hangs 15 January to 27 February 2027 and decisions go out on 21 December 2026. Riverside insures work while it is on the premises, to a per-piece limit of $5,000, but delivery, pickup, packaging and all shipping are the artist's cost, and work not collected within 30 days of the close may incur storage fees or be disposed of. — Deadline: December 11, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: Woven Together · Blue Door Art Center
item.description: A juried group show at Blue Door Art Center in Yonkers, curated by Co-Executive Director Luis Perelman and Gallery Director Michele Amaro, built around weaving taken both literally and as metaphor — fibre, paper, metal, wire and rope alongside photography, painting, sculpture and mixed media. The curators describe the theme as connection, layering, community, memory and "the transformation of individual strands into something larger", which leaves room for photographic work about textile and structure as much as for work whose own making is layered or stitched. Entering costs nothing: submission is free and the gallery pays attention to process, noting it may ask for more detail about materials or method during jurying. Money only changes hands if the work is selected — an in-gallery installation fee of $25 per piece for members and $35 for non-members, or $10 and $15 per piece respectively for the online exhibition, so a photographer can place a print in the physical show for $35. The gallery's terms add two costs they do not price, though: the artist pays shipping or delivery, and insures the work against loss or damage for the time it is in the building. Nothing may exceed 24 by 36 inches or 100 pounds, and the work must be the artist's own original. The show hangs 21 November to 19 December 2026, opening with a reception on 21 November from 1 to 6pm. Sales carry a 25% gallery commission for members and 35% for non-members. The same terms take permission, with attribution and no payment, to reproduce selected work in Blue Door's publicity and exhibition books; copyright stays with the artist. Blue Door is a small 501(c)(3) art centre on Riverdale Avenue, exhibiting since 2002 and an ArtsWestchester grantee; its ArtCall listing tags eligibility as local, while the gallery's own call page states no geographic restriction at all. — Deadline: November 8, 2026. Fee: Free ($25–$35 if accepted). Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: 6th Annual Listen to Women Exhibition · Grosse Pointe Artists Association
item.description: A free juried show for teenage artists in metro Detroit, sponsored by the American Association of University Women, Grosse Pointe Branch, and hung by the Grosse Pointe Artists Association in its gallery at The War Memorial on Lake Shore in Grosse Pointe Farms. The brief is narrow in who it is for and wide in what it will take: artists aged 14 to 18 living in Wayne, Oakland or Macomb counties, making work that shares “their thoughts on issues affecting women”. Entry is free — AAUWGP covers the fee outright, so a 14-year-old photographer can enter a juried gallery show at no cost — and there is real money at the end of it: $200 for Best of Show, $150 for second place and $100 for third. Elizabeth Gauthier, a painter, muralist and adjunct professor at the College for Creative Studies, is the juror, with final acceptance resting with her and AAUWGP. Up to three pieces per artist, submitted as JPGs of at least 600 by 600 pixels and no more than 50MB; images must honestly show the nature and quality of the work, and the organisers ask that pieces be photographed evenly lit and without reflections. There is no stated size cap, though gallery space is weighed during jurying and large installation pieces are out, as is anything built from commercial kits, prefabricated models or hobby crafts. Past winners of the exhibition may enter again. Results go out by email on 3 December; accepted work is delivered in person to The War Memorial on Saturday 5 December between noon and 3pm, with two-dimensional pieces mounted on a rigid backing such as foam board or framed and wired for hanging — clip-on and poster frames are refused. The show runs 9 December to 22 January 2027 and work is collected on Saturday 23 January. Work need not be for sale. — Deadline: December 1, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: $200 Best of Show; $150 second; $100 third.

item.title: The Powerhouse Calls: Past, Present & Future · Novado Gallery
item.description: Juried exhibition at Novado Gallery in Jersey City, made with the Jersey City Landmarks Conservancy, built around a single building: the Hudson & Manhattan Railroad Powerhouse, the Industrial Romanesque Revival hall that electrified the tunnels now carrying the PATH trains from 1908 to 1929 and has stood boarded up a few hundred feet from the gallery for most of a century since. The call asks artists to respond to the Powerhouse and to the cultural landscape that grew around it — the Powerhouse Arts District — “literally, abstractly, conceptually, or metaphorically to its history, architecture, neighborhood, and the city’s industrial and cultural evolution”, and the show is explicitly tied to the Save the Powerhouse preservation campaign rather than being a neutral theme. Photography is named in the eligible media alongside painting, drawing, sculpture, video, installation and mixed media. Open to emerging, mid-career and established artists aged 18 or over, with no geographic restrictions; up to three works per artist, each original, related to the theme and available for sale. Accepted work must stay for sale for the run of the show at a maximum retail price of $10,000, and a sale is split 50% to the artist, 25% to the gallery and 25% to the Landmarks Conservancy, with the artist paid by check or Zelle within 15 days of the gallery receiving payment. Two-dimensional work is capped at 48 by 72 inches excluding the frame; three-dimensional at 48 by 60 by 30 inches including any base. Gallery owners Anne Novado and Eleazar Sanchez jury the submissions for quality, originality, relevance and cohesiveness, and may take one, two, three or none of an artist’s works. Entries go in by email with images, a current CV and the fee; incomplete or unpaid submissions are not considered. Accepted artists supply a bio and a statement of roughly 50–150 words each, and the exact accepted work must be delivered — substitutions are refused and work may not be withdrawn before the closing date. Hand delivery is 6–7 December, shipped work arrives 7–8 December, the opening reception is Saturday 12 December 6:30–8:30pm, the show runs to 30 January 2027, and pickup is 31 January: hand-delivered work left after 1 February incurs a $30-per-day, per-artwork storage fee. — Deadline: November 6, 2026. Fee: $25 (up to 3 works). Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: Hyper-Color: Saturated Artworks · Belvedere Tiburon Library
item.description: Juried group exhibition at THE Gallery, the exhibition space inside the Belvedere Tiburon Library in Tiburon, California, for work that turns the saturation up. The gallery wants pieces “where vivid, intense color is the main event: electric hues, bold contrasts, glowing palettes, and pigments pushed to their limits” — abstract, figurative or conceptual alike — and says the whole piece need not be hyper-saturated, so long as bold colour plays a key role somewhere, whether as a dominant palette, a striking focal element or a standout passage that anchors the work. Photography is named in the accepted media alongside painting, illustration, printmaking, textile and mixed media. The show hangs 21 January to 3 March 2027 with an opening reception on 21 January, and the gallery makes a point of its audience: it sits inside a public library, so each exhibition reaches regular gallery visitors and library patrons passing through, which is part of why the organisers think saturated colour suits the room — “it stops people mid-stride” without asking for any art-historical background. Submissions are first juried anonymously by a panel (applicants are asked to cover any signature on the front of the work in their images), after which the exhibition directors curate for a cohesive show. Conditions to read before paying: entry is open to Bay Area artists aged 18 and over; the work must be two-dimensional and original — framed works on paper or stretched canvas, low relief up to five inches deep, no sculpture or suspended work, and no reproductions of work made in another medium, such as a giclée of a watercolour; all work must be for sale, with 70% to the artist and 30% to the gallery; the library is a family destination, so subject matter must suit it; and accepted work is dropped off in person on 15 or 16 January 2027 and collected on 5 or 6 March. — Deadline: November 7, 2026. Fee: $35 (up to 3 works). Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: Analog vs Digital · ArtHaus Hudson
item.description: Quarterly group show at the ArtHaus Gallery, part of ArtHaus Hudson — a Weehawken, New Jersey arts organisation at 4700 Park Avenue that also runs creative workshops, after-school and music programmes. This edition, opening January 2027, is about the meeting of hand and machine: the organisers want “works that contrast, blend, or investigate the conceptual tension between tactile, handmade processes and modern, pixel-based, or computer-generated practices.” Photography is named in the eligible media alongside painting, drawing, printmaking, digital art, illustration, collage and mixed media, which makes this one of the few calls where an analogue print and a digitally made image are the point rather than a category problem. Two things to weigh before applying: the show is deliberately small — a maximum of ten artists are accepted — and sculpture and freestanding three-dimensional work are excluded outright, so every submission must be wall-mountable and arrive ready to hang with wire or D-rings (unframed canvases need clean or painted edges). All work must be for sale; the gallery retains a 30% commission, so the artist receives 70% of the retail price. The application is a short form on the gallery's own page — bio, medium and links to the work — and the $15 non-refundable fee is paid separately by Zelle with the applicant's name in the payment notes. — Deadline: December 1, 2026. Fee: $15. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: 2027–2028 Gallery Season · Pump House Regional Arts Center
item.description: Annual juried call that fills a whole exhibition year at the Pump House Regional Arts Center, a non-profit arts centre in an 1880 city water pumping station in downtown La Crosse, Wisconsin, converted to a cultural centre in 1977. Accepted artists are scheduled into one of three galleries for a show somewhere between 1 September 2027 and 31 August 2028; the largest, the Kader Gallery, has about 100 linear feet of wall split across two facing walls so that two 2-D artists are often featured at once. The call is open to all styles and to 2D and 3D work, and photography is named among the accepted media alongside painting, sculpture, printmaking, fibre and mixed media. A jury committee of art professionals, educators, artists and patrons — volunteers serving staggered three-year terms — selects from the applications and tells the gallery curator which opening to offer each artist. Conditions worth reading first: work must have been made in the past two years, be unified in theme, and must not have been shown within a 50-mile radius of La Crosse in the previous twelve months; the artist must not have exhibited in the same medium at the Pump House in the previous five years; all work must be for sale, and the Pump House handles sales and retains a 40% commission, so the artist receives 60%; and artists must be available to deliver and collect their own work. The $25 jury fee is waived outright for current Pump House members (membership starts at $35 a year, $15 for students), and a limited number of jury-fee scholarships are available on request. — Deadline: January 31, 2027. Fee: $25 (free for members). Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: MANIFEST 2026: Reflecting on Collaboration · fstop504
item.description: Third annual juried exhibition from fstop504, a volunteer-run New Orleans nonprofit that puts on free and low-cost photoshoots, workshops and exhibitions for photographers, artists and models out of its community studio, Lapin's Workshop. MANIFEST 2026 is part of the PhotoNOLA festival and hangs at the Contemporary Arts Center, New Orleans, from 5 December 2026 to 14 January 2027, opening on First Saturday with a photoshoot alongside the reception. This year the call widens beyond photography — immersive installation, sculpture, video installation, painting and mixed media are eligible alongside it — in recognition of the people who make the organisation's programming. The theme is collaboration, read broadly: work made with another artist or person, work made with skills learned at an fstop504 or Lapin's Workshop event, a photograph taken at one of those events, or collaboration in a more abstract sense — a muse, another artist, nature, society. Applicants answer at least one question about what collaboration means to them. One condition to read before applying: entry is open to anyone who has attended at least one fstop504 or Lapin's Workshop event, and the organisers point out that there is still time to attend one; photographers who have left New Orleans may still submit if they can arrange shipping or delivery of the work. The $35 fee covers installation materials and marketing, and partial or full waivers are available on request if cost is a barrier. Jurors are drawn from the city's institutions: a gallery director, NOMA's curator of photographs, the CAC's executive director and fstop504's founder. — Deadline: October 30, 2026. Fee: $35. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: Fellowship 27 · Silver Eye Center for Photography
item.description: The 27th edition of Silver Eye's annual open call, the Pittsburgh photography centre's programme for recognising "exceptionally talented artists working with photography, particularly those who have not yet received significant recognition or support". Two awards are made: the International Fellowship Award, open to a photographer anywhere in the world, and the Keystone Award for a photographer living in or making work in Pennsylvania, each carrying a $1,000 prize, with two Honorable Mentions of $500 in each category. All six selected artists are included in the Fellowship 27 exhibition at Silver Eye in May 2027 and receive curatorial support to develop the show plus free production support from the Lab @ Silver Eye. Jurors this cycle are Harlan Bozeman, an artist and educator from Central Arkansas whose research-driven practice confronts the erasure of Black legacies, and Dr. Paula V. Kupfer, an art historian and curator from Panama specialising in the history of photography in the Americas, a former managing editor of Aperture now teaching at the University of Pittsburgh. Submissions are a work sample of up to 20 images with a one-page statement, bio or CV and image checklist; photographers featured in a Silver Eye solo or small group exhibition between January 2022 and December 2026 are not eligible, and anyone shown there before 2022 must submit a significant creative departure. Awardees are announced in January 2027. — Deadline: November 19, 2026. Fee: $40. Prize: $1,000 ×2 + $500 ×4 + Exhibition.

item.title: Reflections · The 203 Art Space
item.description: A themed November group show at The 203 Art Space, a contemporary gallery and creative hub on the fifth floor of the Stamford Town Center mall in Connecticut, which mounts a new exhibition every month and runs workshops and community events alongside them. For REFLECTIONS the gallery asks what it means "to reflect, remember, observe, experience, and understand", and invites work that reads reflection in any of its senses — a memory, an emotion, a moment of realisation, a cultural experience, a personal journey, or an artist's reading of the world. The themes it lists are life, nature, identity, memory, society, relationships, transformation and personal experience, approached "through personal experience, observation, imagination, or interpretation". All mediums are welcome, and photography is one of the five media the entry form names, alongside mixed media, painting, sculpture and digital art. This is a physical, hand-delivered show: selections are announced the day after the deadline, work is dropped off at the gallery on 31 October and 1, 3 and 4 November, and the exhibition runs 6 November to 5 December 2026. — Deadline: October 29, 2026. Fee: From $50. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: James Alan Cox Foundation Scholarships for Student Photojournalists 2026
item.description: A free, long-running scholarship program for student photojournalists, run by the foundation set up in memory of photojournalist Jim Cox. This cycle awards five $2,500 scholarships to college or technical-school students — four for video work and one for still photography — a sixth $2,500 scholarship to a graduate student for video, and five digital SLR cameras to high-school students, who submit still photographs only. Awards are paid to the student's school and must be used at the start of the next semester. The foundation is explicit about what it wants and does not want: work that "tells a story", broadly defined — breaking news, sporting events, a graduation, a scientific experiment, an emergency response, an unsolicited act of kindness — and emphatically not art photography: "please don't ruin your chances of being considered by entering images of flowers, glamour shots or kittens". Still-photography applicants submit five images (JPEG or PNG, max 2500 px on the long side, 4 MB); video applicants submit two clips of up to three minutes. The full application also asks for a brief essay, two letters of reference, a school transcript and financial data, and a parental release form for applicants under 18. Applicants must be US citizens at a school in the United States (US citizens at US government schools abroad may apply), must have completed at least one year at an accredited institution, must have taken photography or photojournalism coursework, and must have at least one semester remaining when the award is made. A student may hold only one Cox Foundation scholarship in a year. Applications are open from 15 July 2026 to midnight on the evening of 15 November 2026, and awards are announced in early to mid-December. The foundation has granted more than $380,000 to 209 students across eighteen rounds. — Deadline: November 15, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Six $2,500 scholarships + five DSLR cameras.

item.title: Untitled 21: SooVAC's 21st Annual Juried Show
item.description: The 21st edition of Untitled, the flagship annual juried exhibition of Soo Visual Arts Center — a Minneapolis nonprofit art space founded in 2001 that has shown more than 3,900 under-represented artists and states a focus on emerging artists and on work that challenges and expands conventional notions of aesthetics. Each year SooVAC invites guest jurors with local, national and international reputations to select work from open submissions; the guest jurors for Untitled 21 are Bo Young An and Robert Cozzolino. The gallery frames the series as a chance to work in a professional art space with influential art figures toward an exhibition with a highly regarded reputation, accepts all media from artists at any stage in their careers, and selects directly from the submitted work samples — so the work must be available for exhibition rather than proposed. The submission fee is $25 and the general submission form opens 4 November 2026. The fee-waived form for current SooVAC donors that was live in mid-October is no longer listed: as of 19 October 2026 the gallery's Submittable portal reads "There are presently no open calls for submissions" and the donor form's own URL 302s, so there is no route to enter until the general form opens. Both routes close Monday 7 December 2026 at 11:59 PM. Note that the Submittable form's guidelines body has not been updated for this edition — it still carries last year's Untitled 20 text, including a December 2025 deadline, the previous guest juror and the previous exhibition dates — so check the work-sample count and the drop-off and exhibition dates on the form itself before submitting. — Deadline: December 7, 2026. Fee: $25. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: Black & White: Form. Texture. Light. Shadow. · Black Eyes Gallery
item.description: “Black and white is photography at its purest. Take the color away and what remains is the bones of an image: the curve of a shoulder, the grain of weathered wood, a shadow falling across a wall in the late afternoon. Without color to lead the eye, we slow down.” Black Eyes Gallery wants monochrome work of any genre — landscape, street, portrait, experimental, conceptual — for a December show in its Tucson space. Any monochrome process is welcome, including toned prints and digital conversions, but images with selective color are not eligible, and the call is open to photographers 18 and over. Twenty-five images are selected and the gallery prints, professionally mats and frames every one at its own expense, then keeps them in a permanent online archive credited with your name, title and social link. Juried by Douglas Fur, a nationally exhibited Tucson photographer who spent two years at Decode Gallery and is Artist Liaison and Gallery Manager for Tucson Erotica. Up to five photographs for $40, ten for $50, with two reduced $20 places per call for anyone who asks before submitting; any entry that is not selected earns $5 off the next one. Selling is optional, the artist sets the price and the gallery retains 50% on gallery sales. — Deadline: November 20, 2026. Fee: $40/5 images, $50/10. Prize: Group exhibition.

item.title: The Autumn Book · Woofermagazine
item.description: Woofermagazine — an independent photography magazine that began on Instagram in May 2020 and now carries over a million tagged images — is selecting photographs for its next collective photobook. Autumn is the brief, read through content or aesthetics rather than literally: the call asks for images that carry autumn’s feeling, naming freedom, intensity, stillness, escape and transformation as ways in. Colour and black and white are both welcome. A selection of submitted work is published in the book and credited to the photographer. Terms worth reading before you pay: €16 buys one submission of up to five photographs, and you can buy further submissions to send more; all participants receive a digital version of the book (due November 2026) and a 25% discount on the printed edition, but no free print copy and no fee; copyright stays with you, while submitting grants publication in the print and digital editions and sharing on the magazine’s Instagram, including to promote future open calls. 18+, any nationality. — Deadline: October 22, 2026. Fee: €16. Prize: Publication in a collective photobook.

item.title: Suboart Magazine — November & December 2026 Issues
item.description: Independent print magazine seeking emerging visual artists for its November and December 2026 print issues, published as features of two to four pages, Q&As, or longer interviews. Photography, painting, collage, sculpture and installation, illustration, drawing, mixed media, artist books, printmaking and performance/video all welcome. Submit up to 6 images; free to apply, with a non-refundable €30 participation fee only on selection, waived for between one and five selected artists per issue with preference given to artists from lower-income countries. All selected artists receive a free digital copy of their issue and an image of their pages. — Deadline: October 31, 2026. Fee: Free (€30 if accepted). Prize: Publication.

item.title: JRNL Magazine Winter/Spring 2027 Issue · FotoFilmic
item.description: JRNL is FotoFilmic's recurring authorial photography magazine, welcoming all lens-based contemporary practices from film and alternative or historical processes to digital photography and the hybrid methods between them. Its publishing brackets are deliberately wide, from the personal and everyday to integral studies of critical importance. Submit 10 to 25 images from a single series or cohesive body of work, made January 2017 or later. AI-generated imagery cannot be entered: "JRNL submissions are open to all types of photographic work (film, analog and digital). Please note however that no AI-generated imagery can be entered in JRNL calls." Nine photographers will each receive nine full spreads (18 pages) in the A4-format issue plus a complimentary print copy; the issue launches at a Tokyo party in March 2027. — Deadline: December 14, 2026. Fee: $35. Prize: Publication (9 spreads) + print copy.

item.title: 2027 CPAC Open International Call for Photography — MOP Denver · Colorado Photographic Arts Center
item.description: Selected photographs will be projected onto the Daniels & Fisher Tower on 16th Street Mall in downtown Denver, as part of Night Lights Denver, every evening through March 2027 — the full run of the biennial Month of Photography Denver festival. Horizontal images can instead be programmed onto the Denver Theatre District's new LED screen in Skyline Park. The theme is open-ended and photographers of every skill level are invited: film, scanner, screen-capture, digital camera and any form of mobile photography are all eligible, with no video. Work for the clocktower should be vertical. Submit up to three images; CPAC Executive Director and Curator Samantha Johnston makes the final selection. — Deadline: January 8, 2027. Fee: $10. Prize: Month-long projection exhibition.

item.title: 2027 Pacific Northwest Drawers · Blue Sky Gallery
item.description: Blue Sky, Oregon Center for the Photographic Arts, marks twenty years of its Pacific Northwest Drawers programme — a juried public archive of original prints by up to 60 regional photographers, held in accessible flat-file drawers at the gallery for a full year. This is the rare exhibition where visitors are encouraged to handle the art, and the drawers draw students, curators and collectors as well as daily visitors. Submit exactly ten unwatermarked prints from a single series or body of work, ideally made in the last five years; accepted work must arrive matted or mounted and must not exceed 20 x 16 x 1.5 inches when stacked. Shana Lopes of SFMOMA juries. All accepted work is featured on Blue Sky's website and stays in the digital archive indefinitely; prints are eligible for sale with the artist's permission at a 50% gallery commission. Free to enter, one entry per artist. — Deadline: December 18, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Year-long flat-file exhibition.

item.title: Integration: Genesis from Synthesis · Gather Center
item.description: Gather Center is a 501(c)3 arts and education nonprofit in Greenpoint, Brooklyn, founded in 2023 by Allison Harrell Mistier and André-Philippe Mistier and opened to the public in 2025 with a gallery, digital immersion spaces and a garden. Its programme runs on an annual “Consciousness Spiral” — Awakening in spring, Resonance in summer, Integration in autumn, Embodiment in winter — and this is Phase III. The call asks for work on Integration as “a movement of dynamic stillness, metabolism and revealing interconnections”, which the centre glosses with its own meditations: “The leaf nourishes the seed”, “Through the cracks came the light”, “Slow down to receive”. The framing is openly esoteric — “becoming borderless”, “point of permeability”, transmutation — and the gallery is explicit that it wants interconnection made visible rather than a literal illustration of the theme. Eligibility is open to all artists 18 and over with no location restriction, and the accepted-media list names photography alongside painting, works on paper, textile, sculpture, sound, music, multimedia and performance. One $35 fee covers up to three works. Wall works may run to 60 inches on any side and 40 pounds, projecting no more than six inches, and must arrive ready to hang on wire, D-rings or a cleat — no Velcro, adhesive strips, sawtooth hangers or tape; works on paper must be framed or glazed. The practical gate is physical, not geographic: selected work must be hand delivered to and collected from 94 Guernsey St in person, with drop-off on 18 November 2026 and pickup on 8 January 2027, so shipping is not an option. Notifications go out by 13 November, installation is 19 November, the opening reception is Friday 20 November 2026, 5.30–8.30 PM, and the show stays up through early January 2027, open Saturdays 12–5 PM. Selected audio may also join a companion online release, as the centre did with Resonance. — Deadline: November 8, 2026. Fee: $35. Prize: Group exhibition.

item.title: Man or Bear: No Safe Choice · Woman Made Gallery
item.description: Woman Made Gallery takes the viral question — alone in the woods, would you rather meet a man or a bear — and builds a spring exhibition out of what it exposed. The call is explicit about its subject: “male violence and abuse against women” as it is organised and amplified online, from “the undercurrents of red-pilling young boys and online stalking” to “AI-produced revenge porn, the trans-vestigation of female athletes, manosphere gaming culture, and disinformation smear campaigns of women in positions of power”. Its closing line sets the tone of what the gallery wants: “Both are wild, but at least a woman will be believed when she is attacked by a bear.” The published areas of inquiry are deliberately wide — critique of the manosphere, incel culture, online gender investigations targeting trans people, frat and rape culture, “reclamation of authorship, narrative power, and cultural agency”, intersectional experience across gender, race, class, sexuality, disability and migration, and art as a site of resistance — and the gallery asks for “your most raw reactions over a plethora of mediums and forms”. Submissions are open to women and nonbinary artists at all career stages “working in any medium”; stills and moving image are both accepted at upload. Selection is by MA students from the School of the Art Institute of Chicago rather than a single named juror. Entry is $30 for one to three works, with up to two entries per artist, and WMG publishes reduced fees and fee waivers reserved for BIPOC and LGBTQIA+ artists on request. Work previously shown at WMG is not eligible, nothing may exceed 6 feet on its widest side or 75 pounds unless the artist handles delivery and pickup personally, artists arrange and pay for shipping to the gallery, and sales carry a 40% commission. — Deadline: January 23, 2027. Fee: $30 (waivers available). Prize: Group exhibition.

item.title: International Residency of Experimentation 2027 · Experimental Photo Festival
item.description: Six artists from different parts of the world come to Barcelona for eight intensive days of experimentation, shared learning and hands-on work in the week before Experimental Photo Festival 2027. The structure is horizontal rather than taught: each resident shares an experimental process with the group through one theoretical and practical session — two hours of theory, four of practice — and takes part in the sessions proposed by the other five, so knowledge moves from one artist to another, one cultural perspective to another and one process to the next. The residency is conducted in English so that all six can work in a common language, and it is aimed at artists willing to share what they know and curious about other people's practices. Residents stay at the Col·legi Major Penyafort-Montserrat and work across the residency spaces and the Centre Cívic Pati Llimona. During the festival itself, a collective exhibition presenting the process developed in the residency opens at Pati Llimona alongside a Residency Conference where the residents discuss what they worked on. APPLYING IS FREE, BUT A SELECTED PARTICIPANT PAYS €500, and the festival publishes the breakdown: accommodation €330, materials €30, bank and platform fees €30, and 21% tax €110, with payment possible in monthly instalments; the Association says it pays the residency director's salary from a public grant. That €500 covers the eight nights with breakfast, the materials for the workshops and collective experimentation, access to Experimental Photo Festival 2027, participation in the residency talk and exhibition, official festival merchandise, and a free place on the Diploma in Experimental Photography at Ágora, School of Experimentation, which the festival values at €999. It does not cover accommodation during the festival days, meals other than breakfast, travel or personal expenses. Continuing through the festival is optional and encouraged: a resident who adapts their residency workshop into a four-hour festival format can attend two workshops of their choice free, has their workshop materials provided, and gets meals on the days they work as a festival artist. Applications are reviewed by the Experimentalphotofestival Association together with residency coordinator Célica Véliz — a visual artist and photographer trained in photography, visual arts and ceramics, professor of Photochemical Processes I and II in the University Photography Programme at the National University of La Plata, and director of this residency since 2023 — and consider each artist's proposed practice and process and their ability to share it. An application is a biography of 250 to 500 words, a PDF portfolio, ten JPGs, a portrait, and a workshop proposal form listing materials costed for six people and the space the session needs. — Deadline: November 7, 2026. Fee: Free to apply (€500 if selected). Prize: 8-day residency + Exhibition.

item.title: Experimental Photo Festival 2027 — Artists Open Call
item.description: The eighth Experimental Photo Festival runs in Barcelona from July 21 to 25, 2027, and this is the call for the artists who build its programme — distinct from the festival's exhibition call. It is international and aimed at photographers, visual artists, multidisciplinary artists and collectives who explore, question or transform photography through technique, materials, concept, technology or interdisciplinary practice; the festival says you do not have to call yourself an experimental photographer to apply. A proposal is not a portfolio submission: each applicant proposes two workshops — one of four hours, built on a technique, process or methodology they know well, and one of eight hours that lets participants go deeper into a process, research or experimental approach — plus one discursive activity, either a conference, a roundtable or a project or research presentation, lasting 20 to 40 minutes. Each workshop carries a materials budget of up to €50 covered by the Experimentalphotofestival Association, and an exhibition proposal may optionally be included. Applying is free: the proposal form is a document downloaded from the festival's own call page and submitted through its online form together with a biography of up to 250 words in the applicant's own language, a PDF dossier, ten JPGs of the work and a portrait. SELECTED ARTISTS ARE PAID, AND CHOOSE BETWEEN TWO COMPENSATION OPTIONS: six nights in the festival's official accommodation (stated value €300) plus €200 in cash, or €500 in cash with accommodation arranged and paid by the artist. Either option also includes meals during the festival, full artist accreditation, official 2027 merchandise, and a place on the twelve-month Diploma in Experimental Photography at Ágora, School of Experimentation — more than 60 techniques and processes, specialisation, mentoring and a final personal project — which the festival values at €999. Travel to and from Barcelona is not covered, and payment requires an invoice issued in the artist's name. The festival publishes a financial transparency page stating that 94 people receive compensation through it — 50 artists, 14 staff and 30 volunteers — while 150 people pay a registration fee to attend. Selection is by the Experimentalphotofestival Association team against three criteria: connection to the festival's three challenges (combining knowledge and processes, building meaning beyond technique, and treating creation as a space for exchange), contribution to gender balance in the programme, and originality; applications are read individually and then weighed collectively against the whole 2027 programme. Selected artists must be in Barcelona from July 20 to 26, 2027, with July 20 given to workshop preparation, material review and technical checks, and sign an agreement covering activities, compensation, production, cancellation and image rights. Artists retain copyright and ownership of their work; the Association takes a non-exclusive right to reproduce submitted images, always credited, for promotion, exhibition and editorial use, and to record the festival itself. The call opened October 12 and selected artists are announced in December. — Deadline: November 7, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: €200–€500.

item.title: Upside down · PH21 Gallery
item.description: Curated international group photography exhibition built on a single experimental hanging decision: the photographs are shown turned upside down. PH21's premise is that inverting an image strips it of its representative function — the depicted scene and objects become difficult, if not impossible, to recognise — while the formal and compositional aspects become more pronounced, directing attention away from scene and object recognition. Any photograph is eligible if the artist is willing to present it this way. Abstract photographs may be the most obvious candidates, but the call argues that depictive works can be appreciated in novel ways when inverted, and names landscapes, bodyscapes, symmetrical compositions, architectural and street photography as excellent candidates, with other genres also considered. The theme is broadly interpreted and independent of generic or stylistic constraints. Curated by Zsolt Bátori (PhD in Philosophy, Rutgers; founder, director and curator of PH21 Gallery, a Photolucida Critical Mass juror since 2023 and invited to Photolucida's Board of Directors in 2026) and Borbála Jász (art historian and philosopher of art, PH21 vice-director, a Critical Mass juror since 2025 and also invited to the board in 2026). One curator's choice and up to three honourable mentions are announced; the juror's choice receives three free entries to any upcoming PH21 themed group call, each covering up to 15 images. Entrants may submit 3, 5, 7, 10 or 15 images — individual works, or including a series of at most five photographs — by email after paying the fee. THE STANDARD FEE IS PRICED BY IMAGE COUNT AND RISES AFTER THE EARLY BIRD DEADLINE: until November 30 it is €25 for the first 3 images, €30 for 5, €35 for 7, €40 for 10 and €45 for 15; after November 30 every rung goes up €5, to €30 / €35 / €40 / €45 / €50, so the stored €25 floor is only available up to the early bird date and only for three images. A reduced rate of €15 (early bird) or €20 after it covers up to five images for students, unwaged persons and applicants from low-income economies — the gallery asks for no proof of eligibility and says it trusts the applicant's judgement. Early bird deadline November 30, final deadline December 7; all entrants are notified 10–15 days after the final deadline. The exhibition runs February 6 – March 2, 2027 at PH21's venue in Barcelona's Gothic Quarter. Selected photographers pay a print and installation fee, from €45 for a matted print up to 40cm / 15.75in on the longest side, or may ship their own exhibit-ready prints; entering grants the gallery a non-exclusive promotional and exhibition licence with no royalties, copyright and ownership stay with the photographer, submitted work need not be for sale, and the gallery commission on any sale is 25%. — Deadline: December 7, 2026. Fee: €25–€50. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: True Blue · Cultural Center of Cape Cod
item.description: The Cultural Center of Cape Cod, a 501(c)(3) arts centre on a historic campus at 307 Old Main Street in South Yarmouth, Massachusetts, is running True Blue as an online juried exhibition: from the vastness of the sky to the depths of the sea, from loyalty and friendship to sorrow and melancholy, it asks artists to explore the colour, symbolism and emotional resonance of blue, and it wants interpretations ranging from the literal to the figurative. Photography is named in the eligible media alongside painting, drawing, digital art, mixed media, sculpture, fibre art, printmaking, glass, wood, ceramics and signed, numbered limited-edition prints; video is the only exclusion. Entry is $20 for the first work and $5 for each additional work up to a maximum of 20 images, non-refundable and no guarantee of acceptance. Awards are $300 for first place, $200 for second and $100 for third, and the first-place winner also has the option of showing the winning image — and possibly more, depending on size — for a month during 2027 in the Center's physical Showcase Gallery on the Cape Cod campus, which turns an online prize into a real wall. The virtual exhibition stays online for three months. Jurying is by the Cultural Center's directors, who give no individual feedback. Sales inquiries are routed to the artist, whose own link sits beside the image in the online gallery, and the Center takes no commission on an online sale; in exchange, entering grants the Cultural Center copyright in the image for display and promotional use, while the physical artwork stays the artist's property. Work that is copied, produced by AI, or made under an instructor's guidance is not eligible. Winners are notified and the online gallery opens by December 15, 2026. — Deadline: November 30, 2026.
